Q: Push local Git repository to new remote including all branches and tags A:

The man page for git-push is worth a read. Combined with this website, I wrote the following in my .git/config file:

[remote "origin"]
    url = …
    fetch = …
    push = :
    push = refs/tags/*

The push = : means "push any 'matching' branches (i.e., branches that already exist in the remote repository and have a local counterpart)", while push = refs/tags/* means "push all tags".

So now I only have to run git push to push all matching branches and all tags.

Yes, this is not quite what the OP wanted (all of the branches to push must already exist on the remote side), but it might be helpful for those who find this question while googling for "How do I push branches and tags at the same time?".

Q: Extend CodeIgniter SELECT query containing JOIN and GROUP BY and SUM() to also fetch the latest record in each group A:

Add the whole records with the latest id per group using a couple of JOINs; the first to identify the records, then the second to acquire the whole record that relates to each qualifying id. This can all be done with window function syntax in more modern MySQL versions. SQLize Demo

SELECT
    sh.*,
    SUM(all_rents.paid) total_paid,
    latest_rents.balance current_balance
FROM student_hostel sh
JOIN rent all_rents ON all_rents.stud_id = sh.id
JOIN (
    SELECT stud_id, MAX(id) id
    FROM rent
    GROUP BY stud_id
) latest_rent_ids ON latest_rent_ids.stud_id = sh.id
JOIN rent latest_rents ON latest_rents.id = latest_rent_ids.id
WHERE sh.hostel = 12
    AND all_rents.date = '10-2016'
    AND sh.status NOT IN ('R','G')
GROUP BY sh.id

Query builder:

public function rent_outstanding(int $hostel, string $date): array
{
    $sub = $this->db
        ->select('stud_id')
        ->select_max('id')
        ->group_by('stud_id')
        ->get_compiled_select('rent');

    return $this->db
        ->select('sh.*, latest_rents.balance current_balance')
        ->select_sum('all_rents.paid', 'total_paid')
        ->join('rent all_rents', 'all_rents.stud_id = sh.id')
        ->join("($sub) latest_rent_ids", 'latest_rent_ids = sh.id')
        ->join('rent latest_rents', 'latest_rents.id = latest_rent_ids.id')
        ->where_not_in('status', ['G', 'R'])
        ->group_by('sh.id')
        ->get_where(
            'student_hostel sh',
            [
                'sh.hostel' => $hostel,
                'all_rents.date' => $date
            ]
        )
        ->result();
}

Q: Should a C++ logger write method be defined as const? A:

A const method is not one without side effects.

For example, a const method of a class can change global variables. A const method can also, notionally, create a file containing the content of "War and Peace".
